summary: Outpost Seven: Beyond Earth is a browser-based junior astronaut trainer. Players run a lunar outpost, make four-option crew decisions and carry out repairs and science tasks in a walkable world. Finite supplies make planning matter. An archived NASA DONKI event and NASA/JPL reference values connect the missions to space science. Guided practice, consequences and replay support learning.
details:
Outpost Seven: Beyond Earth addresses Build a Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer by making outpost engineering trade-offs playable for young learners. The goal is a player who can explain a decision and its consequences.

Players practise a compressed space approach and lunar landing, then explore a base with enterable facilities. Oxygen, water, food, power and materials connect fieldwork to base planning. Each standard shift has one main radio call per half, with four options. Reading and decision screens pause the world. Some choices require a physical task, such as operating valves, repairing a connector or installing recovered equipment. Handover shows the resulting reserves and next-shift forecast.

Equipment drills unlock useful tools. Samples feed an observation-and-memory exercise. Emergencies and earned upgrades encourage further practice. CAPCOM exercises teach reporting and delayed replies; completed Moon objectives unlock a Mars training chapter. Optional fictional cave opponents make expedition supplies and returning cargo matter.

NASA resources inform the science lessons, while health points, shielding effects, resource rates and travel compression remain illustrative game rules. Reports and a final assessment record in-game performance. Student playtesting and before-and-after questions are planned to evaluate learning and retention.

The game uses HTML, CSS, JavaScript and Canvas, with browser saves and an offline HTML copy. The source retains an earlier pre-event practice prototype and a teammate-supplied Beyond Earth prototype. Contributions and ChatGPT/Codex assistance are documented; this submission does not claim that all source code originated during the event.
